manufacturer_data.description: Manufacturer-specific advertising data starts with 0x54 0x52 0x00 0x4E. This is the official app's only scan filter (BleConfig.matchProduct matches these four bytes at the start of the manufacturer-data AD structure; the app never matches on local name). App-derived, not hardware-verified.

ble.notes: mask-go discovers masks by local-name prefix "MASK" (names look like "MASK-XXXXXX", last 6 MAC-derived) — a secondary discovery signal used by open-source clients; the official app does not use it (it filters on the manufacturer-data prefix above).

device.name: Shining Mask
device.notes:
LED face mask with 2074 RGB LEDs, 16-pixel-tall display. All commands to the Command characteristic are AES-128 ECB encrypted with the fixed key 32672f7974ad43451d9c6c894a0e8764 (published verbatim in four independent sources: GoneUp/mask-go, BishopFox/shining-mask, BrickCraftDream/Shining-Mask-stuff, Staars' gist). No pairing/authentication. Image data to the upload characteristic is sent unencrypted. FCC ID: 2AOLN-16. Color order for the FC (foreground color) command is R,G,B — confirmed by the official app (Agreement.getTextColor emits the channels in argument order and TextEditActivity passes Color.red/green/blue into it), matching every public implementation (mask-go, tayred06, BrickCraftDream). The earlier R,B,G reading rested on a misread of private APK analysis and is dead; no hardware A/B test is needed for the ordering question. CONFIDENCE: command structure, AES key and FC color order HIGH (official app static analysis agrees with the open-source shining-mask implementations, package cn.com.heaton.shiningmask). Security: Bishop Fox ("Invasion of the Face Changers", 2025-10-30) showed anyone within ~10 m can take over a mask; no fix is expected (no firmware-update channel). Caveat: the v1.2.6 app bundles a dormant Panchip OTA stack (com.cdbwsoft.library.panchip, with its own OTA service/characteristic UUIDs in BleManager) — in this build it is only used to negotiate MTU on connect and no OTA flow is wired to any UI, so whether retail firmware accepts OTA updates is unknown (app-derived, unverified). Hardware RE (adrihd/ShiningAppMask-ReverseEngineering, 2026-01): Artery AT32F415 MCU, Jieli BP27387 BLE SoC, 16 MB PY25Q128HA SPI flash. Decrypted OTA firmware images (TR1906R04-*) and a full flash dump are archived in the research repo (/home/claude/research/shining-mask/firmware/).
Enrich-branch evidence: the official Shining Mask Android package cn.com.heaton.shiningmask was inspected from APKPure XAPK v1.2.6/versionCode 126, SHA256 29cc2c088634b28b06b67cab7b17f15bb6551bdb3d422b4e188274c825fbcb94. Static analysis and public RE agree on service 0000fff0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb holding the d44bc439 characteristics: command d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129600, notification characteristic d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129601, image/text upload characteristic d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-92541612960a, audio visualizer characteristic d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-92541612960b, and CCCD 00002902-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Public sources include GoneUp/mask-go, BrickCraftDream/Shining-Mask-stuff, BishopFox/shining-mask, the Bishop Fox Bluetooth LED mask write-up, and Staars' Shining Mask gist. Text/bitmap upload uses an encrypted DATS start command, DATSOK/REOK acknowledgements, 98-byte chunks when MTU is set and an 18-byte fallback when MTU negotiation has not completed (both chunk sizes confirmed in the app's TextAgreement and DiyAgreement), and DATCP/DATCPOK completion — all app-confirmed. The local XAPK was re-hashed and matches the SHA-256 above, settling the mirror re-signing question.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control — Bishop Fox (2025-10-30) demonstrated unauthenticated takeover within ~10 m, and no fix is expected (the device has no firmware-update channel).

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Commands are AES-encrypted with a fixed key, so any client that implements the framing can connect straight away.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

play_builtin_animation.description: Play built-in animation (0x00-0x45, 70 animations). Layout [0x05, "ANIM", id] app-confirmed (Agreement.getAnimCommand).

set_background_color.description: Set text background color. The command word is "BC" (0x42 0x43), not "BG" — confirmed in the official app (Agreement.getTextBgColor). Same layout as FC: length 6, enable flag at byte 3, channels in R,G,B order. Note the app halves each background channel value (× 0.5) before sending — app-derived behavior, not hardware-verified.

set_foreground_color.description: Set text foreground color. Channels are emitted in R,G,B order — as the template below states — confirmed by the official app (Agreement.getTextColor writes the channels in argument order and TextEditActivity passes Color.red/green/blue), matching every public implementation (mask-go SetTextFrontColor, tayred06 mask_controller.py, BrickCraftDream ble-protocol.md). Byte 3 is an enable flag (1 = apply color, 0 = disable).

set_mode.description: Set display mode. 0=off, 1=steady, 2=blink, 3=scroll R-to-L, 4=scroll L-to-R, 5=steady custom. The 1/2/3/4 mapping is app-confirmed (TextEditActivity maps its steady/blink/scroll UI options onto MODE values 1, 2, 3 and 4).

show_builtin_image.description: Display built-in static image (0x00-0x69, 106 images). Layout [0x05, "IMAG", id] app-confirmed (Agreement.getImageCommand).

characteristics.name: Command
characteristics.notes: onEncrypt() AES-128-ECB with a fixed key is applied before every write to this characteristic. The key is published verbatim in four independent sources (GoneUp/mask-go aes.go, BishopFox code.py, BrickCraftDream ble-protocol.md, Staars gist) and is also embedded raw in the official app's native crypto library (libAES.so, arm64-v8a split of XAPK v1.2.6, key bytes at file offset 0x3008; AES runs in JNI via csh.tiro.cc.aes cipher/invCipher). Confidence: HIGH. Command frames are 16 bytes; unused tail bytes are random padding (Agreement.getRandom()), not zeros — a receiver must not require zero padding. Additional app commands beyond the ones templated below (app-derived, not hardware-verified): BC = set text background color (templated below); CHEC = query DIY image count; FACE = gesture face-change settings; PLAY = play a list of DIY images; DELE = delete DIY images; DIY = show a DIY image; TIME = DIY image timestamp sync; LOOA = animation loop toggle; SOUT = exit rhythm/music mode; SMVEW = enter/exit DIY mode with save sub-commands (the wire bytes really spell "SMVEW" — 53 4D 56 45 57 — apparently a vendor typo, not "SAVEW"); MANCP = multi-image upload completion handshake (DATCPOK → MANCP → MANCPOK).

characteristics.name: Notification
characteristics.notes: Notification payloads are AES-128-ECB encrypted with the same fixed key as the Command characteristic — the official app runs every received value through aes.invCipher before parsing (Agreement.getDecodeData). Decrypted payloads are the ASCII handshake responses (DATSOK, REOK, DATCPOK, ERROR=, FACEOK, DELEOK, PLAYOK, TIMEOK/TIMEERR, CHEC count, MANCPOK).

characteristics.name: Image Upload
characteristics.notes: Bulk text/bitmap upload channel — written UNENCRYPTED (the app's writeCharacteristicBy2 path applies no AES; only the handshake commands on the Command characteristic are encrypted). App-confirmed upload state machine: client writes encrypted DATS [0x09, "DATS", total_len_hi, total_len_lo, ...] on the Command characteristic; device replies DATSOK; client streams payload chunks here, each framed [chunk_len, chunk_index, payload...] with 98-byte payload per chunk once MTU 103 is negotiated (18-byte payload fallback before MTU negotiation); device replies REOK per chunk; client finishes with encrypted DATCP, device replies DATCPOK (ERROR= on failure). Chunk sizes confirmed in the app's TextAgreement and DiyAgreement.

services.name: Shining Mask Service
services.notes: Advertised primary service holding the d44bc439 command/transfer characteristics — confirmed by the official app's BleManager UUID constants (UUID_SERVICE_TEXT = 0000fff0-... with characteristics ...9600/...9601/...960a/...960b and CCCD 00002902), so the earlier QPP-style standalone d44bc439-...-9600 service theory is dead; both GATT-modeling implementations (GoneUp/mask-go, BishopFox/shining-mask) also place them inside 0000fff0. On connect the app negotiates MTU 103 (requestMtu(100 + 3) via the bundled Panchip OTA manager's MTU helper), which is what selects the 98-byte upload chunk size; before MTU negotiation completes it falls back to 18-byte chunks.
